criterion_scores.reasoning: Checked every numbered spec item against the code: (1) qualifier tier is scoped to incoming-name-with-qualifier only, requires a unique bare-name candidate AND equal website hosts, never resolves bare->qualified (verified in ensure_company's else-branch and the selftest's 'one-directional by spec' case); (2) merge()/revert() never call DELETE, tombstone via metadata.merged_into + edge snapshot, collision edges explicitly kept on the source (409 handling), engagement transferred not copied (source zeroed, pre-mortem item 2's real bug fixed); (3) both substrate.py's Graph.follow()/by_name() and retrieve.py's new follow_tombstone() honor tombstones, and retrieve.py's name-lookup path now de-dupes a tombstone with its target by id (pre-mortem item 11, a genuine gap in the first draft, closed here); (4) identity_probe.py exists, is read-only (verified: only req('GET',...) calls), and is wired into /rigor-review. Cross-checked every PATCH column merge()/revert() write (metadata, engagement_count, relevance_score, entity_id, company_id) against spine_client.ALLOW and the actual market-intel-schema.sql column list -- all valid, no ADR-9 violation. Person matching stays exact (name+company or exact LinkedIn), consistent with ADR-4 D3's 'persons never fuzzy-merged.' Not a full 1.0 because I verified this statically (the FakeGraph selftest and the live dry-runs are the only executions that actually ran; I did not execute the code myself in this offline pass), and because of the minor zero-candidate ambiguity gap noted as a low-severity defect.

All four scoped spec items are present with real coverage: 26 identity-specific selftest cases (grep-verified against the post-merge file, matching the claimed count), the DDL half is explicitly parked with a measured re-trigger rather than silently dropped, and the probe is wired into rigor-review with two value-action-registry rows carrying real thresholds and actions. I decided NOT to apply the dangling-reference completeness cap (see defect) because both missing files are runtime-created ledgers the code already handles as absent-gracefully, consistent with this repo's own established pattern and ADR-8's explicit rejection of placeholder files. Docked slightly for the zero-bare-name-candidate branch being undocumented as intentional, and because I can't independently confirm the claimed 93/93 substrate.py and 37/37 spine_client.py selftest totals beyond the identity-specific subset I could count by hand. [harness cap 0.6: check-refs: referenced file(s) missing]

identity_probe.py sits in .claude/scripts/ alongside its siblings (substrate.py, retrieve.py, spine_client.py, recompute_relevance.py) with the same CLI shape (--selftest, --json). All writes route through Graph (itself routed through spine_client per ADR-9) -- no raw urllib/requests calls anywhere in the diff. platform-constraints.md's tombstone table gained a correctly-formatted row that check-tombstones.py's regex column consumes. value-action-registry.md's two new rows match the existing table's column convention exactly. rigor-review/SKILL.md Step 2 was edited in place rather than duplicated elsewhere. No naming-prefix issues (this is code, not a project skill needing the no-'alex:'-prefix rule).

No tombstoned decision is resurrected (this diff RETIRES merge_topics.py's hard-delete, moving toward the tombstone-only ADR-4 D3 design, the opposite direction of resurrection). No fabricated numbers: every baseline figure in value-action-registry.md (1 person dupe, 3 company/topic twins, 2 host collisions, 0 tombstones) matches the bundle's VERIFIED GROUND TRUTH exactly. Both new registry rows carry explicit threshold->action pairs, avoiding the orphan-metric anti-pattern this rubric explicitly calls out. No hardcoded secrets. The DDL half is deliberately NOT built ('no DDL' scoped decision, re-scoped on measured 0-collision data per the ADR-10 amendment) rather than speculative architecture -- this is the lean, contract-first shape the anti-pattern criterion rewards, not premature generalization. Not a full 1.0 given the two low-severity documentation gaps noted.

Every mutating failure mode fails loud with a specific SystemExit message (merge into a tombstone, dangling merged_into, tombstone chain deeper than TOMBSTONE_DEPTH, source==target, revert on a non-tombstone) -- none of these are silent. The pre-mortem file is unusually honest: it has a dedicated 'What the pass did not cover, on purpose' section and a 'Live proof still owed to Alex' section that explicitly states live merges have NOT been run in production (only dry-run), which is exactly the kind of gap disclosure the rubric rewards and the opposite of the confidence-honesty violation this rubric caps for. identity_probe.py's own docstring claim 'READ-ONLY' is verified true by inspection -- no POST/PATCH/DELETE anywhere in that file. Docked slightly for the one under-commented unconditional PATCH noted as a low-severity defect.

defects.issue: The mechanical pre-pass caps completeness for this and identity-merges.jsonl as missing load-bearing files. I don't think the cap is warranted: both paths are runtime-created audit ledgers that the code (identity_probe.py's print_report/ledger_summary) explicitly branches on 'file absent' and reports as 'no data yet' rather than failing or silently treating it as clean — the same pattern as graph-freeze-overrides.jsonl (tracked empty) and deep-read-gate-failures.jsonl (populated only after first trigger) elsewhere in this repo. ADR-8's own retrospective explicitly rejects creating placeholder files to satisfy a dangling-reference check ('not by creating placeholder files to satisfy the check'), so NOT pre-seeding these two files is the more disciplined choice, not a gap.
defects.fix: No code change needed. If the mechanical check keeps flagging it, teach check-refs.sh to treat paths assigned to a *_LEDGER/*_LOG module constant that is only ever opened in 'a' (append) mode as a known runtime-created class, the same way it already special-cases .state/ and settings.local.json per ADR-8's Increment 1 baseline.

defects.issue: resolve_company_tier's caller only writes to the ambiguity ledger when at least one bare-name candidate exists ('elif cands:'). When an incoming qualified name ('Foo (Bar)') has zero bare-name candidates at all, the row is created silently with no ambiguity note. This is a defensible reading of spec item 1 ('every less-certain case is created AND surfaced') since zero-candidates isn't really a confidence judgment call, it's a plain miss -- but the code doesn't say so anywhere, so a future reader has to reconstruct that this is deliberate rather than an oversight.
defects.fix: Add a one-line comment at the 'if not cands:' path (or next to resolve_company_tier's 'no bare-name candidate' return) stating explicitly that a zero-candidate qualified name is an ordinary create, not a surfaced ambiguity, so the asymmetry with the 1+-candidate branch reads as intentional.

defects.issue: This PATCH is issued unconditionally for company/person/topic merges alike, relying on relevance_score/engagement_count being valid columns on all three tables. That's true (confirmed against market-intel-schema.sql), but neither the inline comment above this line nor the merge() docstring says so -- the comment only reasons about the topic/hub case ('a merged topic leaves the dashboard the same day'), leaving a reader to wonder whether the same line is safe when table='person'.
defects.fix: Extend the comment one clause to note relevance_score/engagement_count are _MI_COMMON columns present on all three mergeable tables, so the unconditional patch is deliberate, not topic-specific code that happens to also run for company/person.
